chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn Rabah, who said: We were narrated by Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah, who said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn Hammad from Zuhayr al-Qurashi from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'r from Abu al-Sakheen al-Arjani, who said: He narrated to me Umar ibn Abdillah ibn Talhah al-Nahdi from his father, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'O Abdillah ibn Talhah, do you not visit the grave of Abu al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I said: 'Yes, we do go to it.' He said: 'Do you go to it every Friday?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you go to it every month?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'How distant you are! Indeed, visiting him is equal to one Hajj and one Umrah, and visiting Abu Ali (peace be upon him) is equal to two Hajjs and two Umrahs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith underscores the spiritual centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt by linking their graves to the major acts of worship. The Imam’s gentle rebuke—'What has made you distant?'—highlights that consistent visitation (Ziyarah) serves as a tangible expression of love and allegiance, equating the grave of Imam al-Husayn with the combined reward of Hajj and Umrah, and Imam Ali’s with two of each.
